newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin Jewish community elects new leadership.
newsitem.headline: Berlin Jewish community elects new leadership.

text.p: Officials of the Berlin Jewish community said on Monday the director of the city's leading Holocaust museum had won an initial victory in a contest to become the group's next leader.

Andreas Nachama, 45, director of Topographie des Terrors, the museum of Hitler's Gestapo secret police, topped the list of candidates with 1,950 votes in Sunday's election for the community's representative board.
The community leader will be elected from among the newly selected board members in a second round in a few weeks.
Nachama has been an outspoken advocate for a national memorial for Jews murdered in the Holocaust, a proposed project that has divided the country for nearly a decade.
He is the son of Estrongo Nachama, the chief cantor of the Berlin Jewish community.
Candidates described the election as a battle between generations, ethnic groups and political orientations that have created rifts among Berlin Jews in recent years.
"(The winners) were overwhelmingly younger and more western-oriented intellectuals," historian Julius Schoeps told German Radio.
Schoeps, who also won a seat on the board, added that this group included representatives from the first wave of Soviet Jews who emigrated to Germany during the 1970s.
Current director Jerzy Kanal, 75, did not stand for the election and will retire this year.

The Berlin Jewish community, the largest in Germany, has expanded dramatically in recent years to nearly 10,000 members, due largely to increased immigration by Jews from Russia and the former Soviet Union.
